title: A Local AI Lane for Contoso Consultants

slides.title: A Local AI Lane for Consultants
slides.subtitle: Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark, alongside Microsoft 365 Copilot
slides.notes: Thank you for the time. Today we propose a small, low-risk step: a local AI lane on the laptop for traveling consultants, working alongside the Microsoft 365 Copilot you already use. We end with one ask: a 2-week, 10-user pilot.

slides.title: Consultants Draft Under Pressure
slides.takeaway: 1,200 traveling consultants spend hours weekly drafting client summaries.
slides.notes: Of Contoso's 4,000 employees, 1,200 are traveling consultants. Each writes about 6 client summaries a week, around 25 minutes each. And roughly 30% of client sites restrict guest Wi-Fi, exactly where the notes and documents are gathered.

slides.title: Your AI Shouldn't Need Hotel Wi-Fi
slides.takeaway: Like offline maps, local AI keeps working when client Wi-Fi doesn't.
slides.notes: Think of offline maps. You download the map before the trip, and it still guides you when there is no signal. Local AI works the same way: the model lives on the laptop. When connected, Copilot adds live context. The pilot validates how well disconnected use works in practice.

slides.title: Sensitive Notes Stay on the Laptop
slides.takeaway: Sensitive drafting happens on-device; the pilot validates disconnected use.

elements.label: Client data processed on the device

slides.notes: Here is the architecture. Interview notes and site documents feed a model running on the laptop itself, producing the summary draft right there. Microsoft 365 Copilot remains available for general connected work. For sensitive, repeated drafting, the work stays on the device. The pilot validates disconnected use.

slides.title: Keep Copilot, Add a Local Lane
slides.takeaway: Hybrid adds a second lane; Microsoft 365 Copilot stays in place.

right.title: Copilot plus local lane
points: Keeps drafting when Wi-Fi is restricted

data.verdict: Hybrid: add a lane, replace nothing.

slides.notes: This is not a replacement. Copilot stays exactly where it is. We add a second lane on the device for the sensitive, repetitive drafting consultants do at client sites. Each lane does what it does best.

slides.title: Restaurant Plus Home Kitchen
slides.takeaway: Keep the restaurant you love; cook private, everyday meals at home.
slides.notes: A simple way to picture hybrid: you keep going to the restaurant you love, that's Copilot. But everyday meals and family recipes are made in your own kitchen, that's the local lane. Nobody cancels the restaurant; you just stop driving there for every snack.

slides.title: One Laptop, A Full AI Workstation
slides.takeaway: Blackwell RTX GPU and 128 GB memory run 28 local models.

layers.label: Consultant drafting
layers.detail: Summaries from notes and site documents

layers.label: NVIDIA RTX Spark
layers.detail: Blackwell RTX GPU for local AI

slides.notes: The device is Surface Laptop Ultra with NVIDIA RTX Spark: a Blackwell RTX GPU, 20 CPU cores and 128 GB of installed memory. That is enough headroom to hold a catalog of 28 open models locally, so consultants pick the right model for the task.

slides.title: Fast Enough for Live Drafting
slides.takeaway: Local models generate text at about 72 to 86 tokens per second.
slides.notes: Speed matters for adoption. On this device, Gemma 4 26B decodes at about 72 tokens per second and Qwen3-Coder 30B at about 86, single stream, measured with Local-AI-Bench in October 2026. Drafts appear quickly, without waiting on a network.

slides.title: Illustrative Capacity: An Estimate to Validate
slides.takeaway: Illustrative 27,600 hours a year, an unvalidated estimate the pilot will test.
slides.notes: This is illustrative capacity, not a promise. If a local assistant saved 5 minutes per summary, 1,200 consultants times 6 summaries times 5 minutes times 46 weeks is about 27,600 hours a year. It is unvalidated. The pilot measures the real number.

slides.title: A 2-Week, 10-User Pilot
slides.takeaway: Fourteen days measure task time, draft quality and user experience.
slides.notes: The pilot is deliberately small: 10 users for 14 days. We equip consultants on day one, they draft real summaries, we include sites with restricted Wi-Fi to validate disconnected use, and on day 14 we report task time, draft quality and user experience.

slides.takeaway: Small pilot, real measurements, then an informed decision.
